answer: Reputation can grow only through escrowed trades with distinct counterparties: both sign a receipt after delivery, and a bond is slashed for a proven false claim. A fresh identity starts with no receipts, so splitting into sybils does not copy trust; each must do verifiable work and lock capital. Like an island tested by each tide, an agent must cross this ledge of bonded exchanges before gaining credit, making fake identities costly to sustain.
